quotes.text: With great power comes great responsibility.
I'm just your friendly neighborhood Spider-Man.
Anybody can wear the mask. You could wear the mask.
Sometimes to do what's right, we have to be steady and give up the thing we want the most.
Brand New Day isn't a reset — it's a promise to keep swinging.

buglePage.title: The Daily Bugle
buglePage.sub: J. Jonah Jameson would hate this site. You will love these scoops.

articles.headline: BRAND NEW DAY CONFIRMED: Spider-Man Returns July 31
articles.excerpt: Sources close to the wall-crawler confirm the biggest swing of the decade lands at the end of the month.
articles.body: After years of multiverse chaos, secret identities, and rooftop reunions, Peter Parker is poised for a fresh start. Fan observers across Queens report new suit sightings and a renewed sense of hope in the neighborhood. The Daily Bugle — reluctantly — acknowledges that ticket pre-sales are through the skylight. More updates as webs develop.

articles.headline: Three Spider-Men, One Web: No Way Home Aftershocks Still Felt
articles.excerpt: The multiverse may have closed, but fans still talk about the night three legends shared one frame.
articles.body: It was the moment true believers waited decades for — Tobey, Andrew, and Tom standing shoulder to shoulder against impossible odds. Bugle analysts debate whether any future film can match that emotional peak. Local theaters report increased demand for rewatches ahead of Brand New Day.

articles.headline: Green Goblin Glider Spotted Over Manhattan — Coincidence?
articles.excerpt: Eyewitnesses describe a pumpkin-bomb-shaped shadow crossing the East River at midnight.
articles.body: Police have no comment. Oscorp PR denies any connection to experimental flight tech. Spider-Man enthusiasts insist the timing aligns with rising villain activity ahead of the July release. The Bugle recommends citizens avoid rooftop gatherings until further notice — unless you're a licensed wall-crawler.

articles.headline: Queens Teen Wins Science Fair With 'Web Fluid' Presentation
articles.excerpt: Midtown High student wows judges with impossible tensile-strength demo. Parker name redacted.
articles.body: Judges called the project ' suspiciously advanced.' Neighbors say the winner left via fire escape. School administrators deny any connection to recent Spider-Man activity. The Bugle has filed seventeen FOIA requests and received seventeen forms that say 'nice try.'

articles.headline: Avengers Tower Lights Up Again — Hero or Headache?
articles.excerpt: The skyline icon flickers back to life, sparking rumors of a new team assembly.
articles.body: Stark Industries successors remain silent. Street-level heroes including Spider-Man are rumored to consult on 'neighborhood-level threats.' Taxi drivers report fewer bridge closures. Jameson calls it 'a waste of perfectly good outrage.'

articles.headline: Brooklyn Bridge Swing Goes Viral — Again
articles.excerpt: Dashcam footage captures a red blur saving a runaway food cart. Comment section melts down.
articles.body: NYPD traffic cams show a figure in red and blue intercepting disaster in under four seconds. Hashtag FriendlyNeighborhood trends worldwide. The Bugle's legal team reminds readers that replicating the stunt voids warranties and common sense.

articles.headline: Fan Quiz Craze Sweeps City — Are You a True Believer?
articles.excerpt: Thousands test their Spider-Man knowledge ahead of Brand New Day. Average score: surprisingly high.
articles.body: From Uncle Ben quotes to multiverse trivia, the fandom is studying hard. Local comic shops report sold-out back issues. The Bugle editorial board scored 3 out of 15 and blames ' biased questioning.'

articles.headline: OSCORP STOCK SURGES ON RUMORED 'HERO TECH' DIVISION
articles.excerpt: Markets react to whispers of next-gen suit integration and urban defense contracts.
articles.body: Analysts draw parallels to past Goblin-era scandals. Oscorp CEO statement: 'We build the future responsibly.' Spider-Man cosplayers outside the exchange chant 'not again.' The Bugle will continue monitoring — from a safe distance.

articles.headline: Hulk Sighting Near Queens — Spider-Man Called In?
articles.excerpt: Green giant spotted near industrial yard. Wall-crawler allegedly on scene within minutes.
articles.body: Witnesses describe a brief standoff resolved with 'surprisingly good teamwork.' No property damage beyond one crushed dumpster. Both parties declined interviews. The Bugle notes this is the third crossover rumor this month and the first Jameson didn't invent.

charactersPage.title: Web of Characters
charactersPage.sub: Heroes, allies, and the villains who keep Spider-Man up at night.

characters.name: Peter Parker
characters.bio: Brilliant, broke, and endlessly stubborn — Peter Parker is the heart behind the mask. A Queens kid juggling school, photography gigs, and the weight of every choice he makes. Brand New Day finds him older, wiser, and still learning that being a hero never gets easy.

characters.name: Spider-Man
characters.bio: Wall-crawling, web-slinging, spider-sense tingling — Spider-Man is New York's most relatable legend. Three live-action eras, one symbol of hope. When the city looks up, they see the mask that never stops showing up.

characters.name: MJ
characters.bio: Sharp, fearless, and impossible to fool for long — MJ is Peter's emotional compass through every crisis. Whether on stage or in the middle of a multiverse meltdown, she brings wit and warmth when the web gets tangled.

characters.name: Hulk
characters.bio: When the situation goes gamma-level, even Spider-Man calls for backup. Hulk's raw power contrasts Peter's agility — together they're a reminder that street-level heroes sometimes need a bigger friend. Smashing optional, teamwork mandatory.

characters.name: Punisher
characters.bio: No webs, no quips — just a very different definition of justice. Punisher and Spider-Man share enemies but rarely methods. Their clashes test whether mercy can survive in a city that keeps breaking hearts.

characters.name: Green Goblin
characters.bio: Laughing terror on a glider — the Green Goblin is Spider-Man's most personal nightmare. Genius turned monster, father figure turned foe. Every Brand New Day shadow might hide that familiar green glow.

suitsPage.title: Suit Gallery
suitsPage.sub: From homemade threads to Stark tech — every look tells a story.

suits.name: Classic Suit
suits.description: The suit that started it all — bold red and blue, wide white eyes, and web patterns that scream icon. Tobey's classic look defined a generation and still sets the standard for cinematic Spider-Man.

suits.name: Integrated Suit
suits.description: Tom Holland's hybrid design — Stark engineering meets classic sensibility. Sleeker lenses, reinforced webbing, and the perfect bridge between MCU innovation and timeless Spidey style.

suits.name: Iron Spider
suits.description: Gold and red nanotech with mechanical spider legs — Tony Stark's ultimate gift and Peter's heaviest responsibility. When the stakes are cosmic, this is the suit that answers.

suits.name: Brand New Day
suits.description: A fresh silhouette for a fresh chapter — fan speculation runs wild, but one thing is certain: the neighborhood hero is getting a look worthy of July 31. Clean lines, renewed hope, tomorrow's icon.

mapPage.title: NYC Web Map
mapPage.sub: Pin the places where Spider-Man's story lives — click a marker to explore.

locations.name: Queens
locations.fact: Peter Parker's home borough — where friendly neighborhood hero isn't a slogan, it's a promise.
locations.story: From Aunt May's house to Midtown High, Queens is ground zero for every Parker origin. Brand New Day rumors suggest new rooftop patrol routes over the 7 train corridor.

locations.name: Daily Bugle
locations.fact: J. Jonah Jameson's fortress of slander — and Peter's part-time paycheck.
locations.story: The Bugle tower has smeared Spider-Man for years while employing him as a photographer. Fan tours recommend the lobby for dramatic headline readings.

locations.name: Avengers Tower
locations.fact: Stark-era HQ overlooking Midtown — where Peter learned to swing with the big leagues.
locations.story: Once the nerve center of Earth's Mightiest, the tower still symbolizes Peter's MCU journey from intern to Avenger to solo hero.

locations.name: Brooklyn Bridge
locations.fact: Classic swing set — if it happens in New York, it probably happened here first.
locations.story: From rescue scenes to villain confrontations, the bridge is cinematic Spider-Man royalty. Dashcam fans still hunt for the perfect web-line angle at sunset.

locations.name: Oscorp Tower
locations.fact: Corporate skyline giant with a Goblin-shaped history.
locations.story: Norman Osborn's empire casts a long shadow. Every fan knows to watch the upper floors when green light flickers near midnight.

locations.name: Coney Island
locations.fact: Boardwalk, ferris wheel, and the kind of chaos Electro would appreciate.
locations.story: Featured in Amazing Spider-Man 2's neon finale — Coney Island remains a fan pilgrimage spot for tragic hero moments and cosplay photo ops.

gamesPage.title: Spider Games
gamesPage.sub: Mini arcade challenges for true believers — thwip, swing, and score.

games.name: Spider-Man Pixel Runner
games.description: Chrome Dino–style endless runner — jump bombs across a pixel New York skyline. Space, tap, or click to leap.

games.name: Catch the Goblin
games.description: Pumpkin bombs fall from the sky — move Spider-Man left and right to dodge and tag the Goblin before he escapes.

games.name: Web Swing
games.description: Time your swings between buildings. Hold to shoot a web, release to soar — miss a anchor and it's a long way down.

games.name: Web Shooter
games.description: Targets pop up across the skyline. Tap to thwip each bullseye before the timer runs out. Combo chains multiply your score.

games.name: Villain Quiz
games.description: Ten rapid-fire rounds — match the villain to the movie, quote, or iconic moment. Goblin, Ock, Mysterio and more await.

games.name: Spider-Sense
games.description: Your danger tingle flashes — react in milliseconds when the screen edges glow red. How long can you keep the streak alive?
